input.goal: Read-only review of four Marionette v5 consumer guides, useful framework-wide teaching without unnecessary helper/example correctness abstractions.
input.currentPlan: Write production, accessibility/rendering, lists, widgets guides. Verify actual JS fences installed; browser keyboard/history/dialog pre-removal checks. Production is prose pointing to existing executed recipes, no live deploy claim.

docs/guides/production.md
docs/guides/accessibility-rendering.md
docs/guides/lists.md
docs/guides/widgets.md
test/docs/list-guide-checks.mjs
test/docs/accessibility-guide-checks.mjs
test/docs/widget-guide-checks.mjs
input.diffSummary: Class scoped Lit/data setup where needed. Local View/Region owners; no added Application or API injection. Native dialog imperative control, optional incomplete data. No dependency/runtime changes. Three new actual JS fences; browser checks running.
input.notes: Local subagents executed their fences; full local merged harness and browser suite pending. Do not assume passed until actual result. Existing reference runtime contracts: View onDomRemove before attached rerender/detach; Behavior direct destroy emits no destroy notification. API docs source available read-only.
input.openQuestions: Any confirmed API/security/architecture inaccuracies, overly strict ownership rules, missing decisive checks, over-explained edge cases, helpers to remove? Focus on scope and concrete correctness; existing reference tests need not be duplicated.

result.verdict: Nearly ready, but don't merge yet. The scope and ownership model are sound, and no Application, API injection or helper abstractions were added. Two things stop the merge: the full harness and browser runs haven't reported results, and one list assertion looks vacuous (it can't fail). Beyond that, the fixes are small corrections and trims.
blockingIssues: The full merged docs harness and the Playwright browser suite are still pending. The decisive claims depend on them: dialog closes before removal, Enter/Space activation, Escape dismissal, and focus kept on the list row. JSDOM covers none of these. Hold the merge until they pass in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.

Test bug in list-guide-checks: the `lateRenders` check patches `current.render` after `modelEvents` were already bound. Marionette resolves string handlers to the function when it binds them (true in v4; please confirm for v5), so the patched function is never what gets called and `lateRenders === 0` passes whether or not listeners were removed. As written it doesn't test the guide's claim that destroyed data "no longer renders the old list". Replace it with a check that can fail, e.g. assert that `current.el.textContent` does not include 'After destruction', or record the row text before `region.destroy()` and compare after.
risks: Anchors are unverified: application.md#preparation-cancellation-and-failure, region.md#showing-a-view, view.md#lifecycle-hooks-and-events, behavior.md#destruction-and-nested-behaviors, tooling.md#look-up-a-diagnostic. External ones too: WAI `#kbd_focus_discernable_predictable`, Lit `#primitive-values` and `#unsafehtml`. Run a link/anchor checker.
The version string `5.0.0-rc.2` is hard-coded in production.md. It will drift unless a docs check ties it to package.json.
production.md writes the Vite target as `baseline widely available`. The actual config value is `'baseline-widely-available'`. Use the literal value or rephrase it.
accessibility-rendering.md says the native DOM provider inserts strings with `innerHTML`. Confirm this against the dom provider source; it is a security statement.

The widget JSDOM check never opens the dialog, so it never shows that `closeDialog` runs from `onDomRemove` or `onBeforeDestroy`. Until the browser check passes, the main claim of the widget guide is unverified.

The HelpView dialog uses `aria-label="Help"` next to a visible `

Help

`. `aria-labelledby` pointing at the heading is the better pattern for an accessibility guide and avoids the name and heading drifting apart.
incorrectAssumptions: Assumption: patching an instance method after construction intercepts `modelEvents` handlers. Handlers named by string are resolved when events are bound, so the patch is never called.

Implied by the widget guide: the JSDOM check covers close-before-removal. It only covers the ownership transitions (render/detach/re-show/destroy and the dom:remove count). The guide's last section says this, but the test file shouldn't be read as evidence for the modal claims.
missingTests: Widget: a JSDOM spy on `closeDialog` showing it runs on render, on `detachView`, and on `region.empty()`, including `onBeforeDestroy` on a View that is already detached. This works without `showModal` and pins the hook wiring.

Widget browser test: `showModal()`, then render/detach/destroy, then assert `dialog.open === false` before the node is disconnected (listen for the dialog's `close` event) and that `document.activeElement` is no longer inside the removed subtree.
Accessibility browser test: real Tab, Enter and Space via Playwright keyboard (not `.click()`), checking `aria-pressed` and that focus stays on the button.

Lists: an assertion that the non-vacuous destruction check could fail (see blocker). Optionally, re-render `catalog` and check that the checkbox resets and `descending` is false, since the guide explicitly claims this.
simplifications: widgets.md: drop the sentence "The bounded query in closeDialog also works when UI bindings are unavailable during teardown", or just use `this.getUI('dialog')[0]` consistently if the UI bindings are still there in onBeforeDestroy. Either way the internal explanation goes.

lists.md: the sentence about assigning `list.collection` not transferring its existing subscription, and the `cid` versus server `id` note, are edge cases for a reference page. Move them to the collection-view reference or cut them.
production.md 'Handle startup at its owner' repeats the Application failure contract. Shorten it to prepareStart/onStart/caller-handles-rejection plus the link.
production.md: collapse the browser-target paragraph to one sentence: the repo tests Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, and you should test your own targets.
nextSteps: Add a JSDOM `closeDialog` spy to widget-guide-checks.mjs; wait for the browser dialog, keyboard and focus results.
Run the anchor/link check and correct the Vite target string.
Check the innerHTML claim against the dom provider source.
Make the optional prose trims above, then re-run the merged harness and merge once it and the browser suite pass.
